preview_strategy_trade_levels.description: Before committing a stop, target or R:R change, see what the strategy's bracket builds on one coin right now, both directions: the setup its one stop and one exit plan build, with each target's price and close %, the stop distance in %, the plan's R:R measured from that stop, and a runner's trail distance in ATR and R — or, when none is built, the refusal with the reason its row describes and the ratio it reached, stated to 3 decimals; the stop, with the verdict its row describes, the bound that refused it and the ATR multiple it was judged at (an ATR stop's own multiple; bounds are inclusive) — the one statement of the stop's distance in ATR; the plan's refused level targets; and the reachable stop band in ATR and %. Every price is on the venue's price grid, rounded once the way its order rests — a stop toward entry, a target away from it, a resting entry away from the mark. The setup's stop and target distances and the entry's distance from the mark are measured between those grid prices and stated to 4 decimals; a stop row's distance is its stop's own figure. Each direction's `entry` is null for an at-market entry; under a level trigger it states the entry on the direction's construction basis — the level read, the placed price, its side of the mark and the order that RESTS there (the construction is built at that placed price), with how far it sits from the mark (distancePct, distanceAtr) and how long it stays valid (validForMinutes), or why it is refused (WRONG_SIDE with the side the order needed; LEVEL_UNREAD, read and absent; INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, too few bars to read the level, with the bars needed and available; READ_NEVER_RAN; ATR_UNAVAILABLE; ATR_INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, the ATR still warming up, with the bars needed and available). `source` is the player's staged draft ({"kind":"DRAFT", strategyId, draftVersion} at the draftVersion get_strategy_draft returned, composed as commit_strategy_draft would compose it — a moved draft is refused with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED) or a committed strategy ({"kind":"COMMITTED", strategyId}). The same computation as the Strategy Studio's preview; writes nothing.

stage.description: `LEVEL_UNREAD`: The entry level has no reading on this bar, so no order can be placed and nothing is built. `INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY`: The platform holds too few bars of this coin to read the entry level, so no order can be placed and nothing is built. It is not a quiet market: the level may exist. `READ_NEVER_RAN`: No read of the entry level ran on this bar, so no order can be placed and nothing is built. `WRONG_SIDE`: The entry order would sit on the side of price it cannot rest on, so nothing is built for this side.

levelReading.description: The reading a LEVEL stop was built from: for a nearest level, its pick among the candidates on the loss side of the entry; on a WRONG_SIDE row, the level's own reading. Null for an ATR or PERCENT stop and on LEVEL_UNREAD, INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY and READ_NEVER_RAN.

verdict.description: `SURVIVED`: Inside your band — this stop can be paired with a target. `BELOW_FLOOR` (`minStopLossAtrMultiple`): Closer to entry than your floor allows on this coin. Lower the floor to keep it. `ABOVE_CEILING` (`maxStopLossAtrMultiple`): Further from entry than your hard stop allows. Widening the hard stop keeps it — and moves the resting order out with it, which buys a smaller position for the same risk budget. `ABOVE_STRUCTURAL_CEILING`: Past the platform cap of 5 × ATR, which applies at every setting — no dial recovers it. `LEVEL_UNREAD`: The level has no reading on this bar, so this stop has no price here. It is never substituted or stretched. `INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY`: The platform holds too few bars of this coin to read the level, so this stop has no price here. It is not a quiet market: the level may exist. It is never substituted or stretched. `READ_NEVER_RAN`: No read of the level ran on this bar, so this stop has no price here. It is never substituted or stretched. `WRONG_SIDE`: This stop sits on the profit side of entry on this bar, so it cannot protect the trade. A nearest level — a zone edge or midpoint, a pool, a naked POC or a single print — looks past its own pick to the next of its kind on the loss side, and is refused only when none sits there, at its own reading. A refused stop builds no setup.
